Team onboarding · October 2026

Utility Optimizer CRM Guide

How to take an energy deal from first contact to Live / Won, and what every screen in the CRM is for. The screenshots follow a TEST deal through the whole journey, on a copy of the CRM with demo users and data, so names such as "Aisling Admin" are examples.

Signing in and the menu

Go to the CRM (uo-crm-web.onrender.com) and sign in with your work email and password (or Microsoft / Google if your administrator set it up). Everyone uses the same screens; you only see the buttons your role allows.

From lead to Live / Won

Every energy deal moves through the same stages. The CRM won't let a deal skip ahead until what each stage needs is in place. If you try, a box lists what's missing: each item is a link, and Take me there opens the first one.

StageBefore you can move hereUsually done by
New Lead → Comparison or Pricing PreparedNothing. Move freely as you call and qualify the lead.Sales
Proposal SentAt least one supply site.Sales
Supplier or Product SelectedThe supplier is chosen. The deal is handed to the back office here.Sales
Documents PreparedA customer record is linked; VAT number if VAT registered; landlord details for rented premises.Back office
SubmittedMPRN/GPRN on every meter, the contract, every required document received and approved, the customer's signature, internal approval. A change of supplier also needs a checked bill.Back office
Awaiting ConfirmationWhat was sent to the supplier is recorded, and the supplier's acceptance with its reference.Back office
Live / WonUse Activate with the start date. The renewal is scheduled automatically.Operations or a manager

Who does what

  • Salespeople add leads, call, qualify, add sites and meters, choose the supplier, and see their own deals and customers.
  • Back office / Operations pick up deals at Supplier Selected: documents, supplier forms, signatures, submission, the supplier's answer and activation.
  • Managers see every deal, approve deals, assign leads and close import batches.
  • Compliance and Finance review restricted documents and bank details.
  • Administrators manage users, suppliers, settings and data retention.

Sales

1. Add a lead

  1. Click New lead (top right on Home) or Leads and deals → New.
  2. Give it a name and choose the service; that's all that's required.
  3. Pick the lead source. Check it: the form starts on Social Media.
  4. Fill in Who is it? with what you know: business, contact, email, phone.
  5. Set a Next action and follow-up date; a first-contact task is created for you.
  6. Click Create opportunity.

Other ways in: scan a business card, or import a CSV list from Leads and deals.

Everyone

2. Move a deal through the stages

The deal page shows the stage bar under the title. Use the green Move to … button for the next stage, or More to jump to any stage. If something is missing, the CRM tells you exactly what.

Sales

3. Supply site, meter and contract

  1. Open the Energy tab and click Add site: the supply address and whether the premises are owned or rented (rented needs the landlord).
  2. Add meter: the MPRN (11 digits starting 10) or GPRN (7 digits). Anything else needs a reason.
  3. Add contract: current supplier, the new supplier, term, rates and proposed start date.
  4. Optional: Add quote under Price comparison for each supplier you priced. Choosing a quote sets the selected supplier and the expected commission.
  5. On Overview, set the Selected supplier. Moving to Supplier Selected hands the deal to the back office.

Sales or back office

4. Link or create the customer

On Overview, the Customer card links the deal to a customer record, or creates one from the details you captured. The CRM warns you about possible duplicates (same email, phone, CRO, VAT, or name and Eircode). It never merges them on its own; managers merge.

Back office

5. The supplier's application form

For Electricity with Flogas or Bord Gáis, the deal gets its own form tab, filled from the deal. Work through its sections, click Validate application, then generate the PDF and Send for signature: the customer gets an email link to sign online.

  • Sector, pricing and rates are optional; rates take up to 2 decimals (1.05 stays 1.05).
  • If the customer signs on paper, use Upload signed PDF on the form instead.
  • A signed form is approved by someone other than the person who sent it or uploaded it.

Back office

6. Documents

  1. The Documents tab lists what this deal needs (energy bill, letter of authority, signed contract, and more for a change of tenancy).
  2. Upload each file (or drag it in). Every upload is kept as a new version and virus-scanned.
  3. Review each one: Approve, or Reject with a note saying what's wrong.
Watch out: uploading a new version, including a signed copy, sends that document back to "Awaiting review". Approve it again before submitting.

Back office

7. Signatures

The Signatures tab is for documents signed outside a supplier form. Request signature, add the customer as a signer, and when they've signed (in person or by returning a scan) use Record signature and attach the signed copy.

Manager

8. Internal approval

Before submission a manager approves the deal. Click Approval on the deal: it lists anything still outstanding, then Approve or Reject with a note.

Back office

9. Submit to the supplier and record their answer

  1. Move the deal to Submitted, then open Back office. The case steps at the top tick themselves from what's recorded.
  2. Send the pack to the supplier, then click Record submission: who it went to, how, the date, the exact files, and the proof of delivery (for example "sent from sales@ at 10:42").
  3. When the supplier replies, click Record response: Accepted with their reference, or Changes required / Rejected with the reason (this creates a correction task).
  4. Then move to Awaiting Confirmation.
Two open deals on one meter? The case warns you when another open deal uses the same supply point, so the same meter isn't switched twice.

Operations or manager

10. Activate: Live / Won

When the supplier confirms the switch, click Activate, enter the start date and the supplier's reference. The deal becomes Live / Won, the contract end date is set, and a renewal deal is created automatically 120 days before it ends.

Everyone

11. Timeline and tasks

Every change, call, email, upload and approval is written to the Timeline automatically and can't be edited or deleted; a correction is a new entry. The deal's Tasks tab holds its calls and to-dos, many created and closed automatically.

Home

For the back office, Home is the work queue: handed-over deals by status (overdue, ready to send, awaiting the supplier, rejected). Below it, the dashboard shows new leads, the open pipeline, won and lost deals, and time to activation, filtered by period, salesperson, service and supplier. Managers can download the commissions CSV here.

Leads and deals

Every opportunity in a searchable list with views (my open deals, all, won, renewals due, awaiting customer or supplier). Tick rows to assign several leads at once (managers). Import brings in a CSV of leads; a whole import batch can be closed as lost, and untouched leads deleted by an administrator.

Pipeline

The board view: one column per stage. Drag a card to move it, or use its menu. If a move is blocked, the same "still needs" box appears with Take me there.

Cases

The back office's list of handed-over deals and their case status (new supply, change of supplier, change of legal entity, renewal), with what each is waiting for.

Customers

Every customer with the same columns as the master sheet: business and trading name, contact, phone, email, MPRN/GPRN, supplier, utility, product, start and expiry dates, status and sales agent. Search by name, email, phone or MPRN/GPRN. A customer's page has their details, contacts, sites, bank details (restricted) and every deal they've had.

My tasks

Your calls and to-dos across all deals, with due dates. Tick them off as you go; the automatic ones (first contact, missing documents, signature chasers, supplier follow-ups, renewals) close themselves when the work is done.

Needs a connected mailbox

Email

Connect your mailbox once (Account page) and customer emails appear here and on each deal's timeline. Reply from the CRM so everything stays on record.

Scan business card

Photograph a business card on your phone; the CRM reads it and creates a lead with the details, checking for duplicates first.

Template managers

Supplier forms

Upload a supplier's PDF form and place its fields once; after that the back office fills it from any deal in one click. Flogas and Bord Gáis electricity forms come set up.

Administrators

Administration

Users and roles, teams, suppliers (with each supplier's submissions email, which fills in Record submission), stages, settings, email signatures, integrations and data retention.

Your account

Click your initials (top right) for your account: change your password, turn on two-factor sign-in, set your phone for click-to-call, connect your mailbox and set your email signature.
